title: Hytale Adaptive Surface: persistent geometry with selected-block materials
summary: Adaptive Surface 0.12.4 on Hytale 0.7.2: user reports the installed release works successfully after the client-side transition orientation correction. Technical evidence covers client pose, negative control and native fixtures; long-duration performance and future client versions remain unverified.
problem_class: adaptive block geometry and selective material texture loading
problem_description: One smoothing block must form slopes/corners, retain its shape/material across world saves, and copy the exact block a player right-clicked without rebuilding a large client atlas during play or preventing world startup.
context: Adaptive Surface 0.12.4 is installed on Hytale 0.7.2, Windows, Java 25. The client yaw-minus-PI correction follows 0.12.3 transition isolation. The user reported on 2026-10-20 that the latest work succeeded and everything works. This is user acceptance of the installed result, separate from the existing technical tests; no instrumented framebuffer or long-duration performance measurement was supplied.
inputs: native cube textures and material variants
constraints: client assets must be registered before join
no runtime asset registrations during placement
one visible creative item and no command
new learned textures become available after restart
known_attempts: full HD catalogue active at startup
placement interaction sync data for clicked material

solution_versions.description: Adaptive Surface 0.12.5 on Hytale 0.7.3: fail-closed world-pack regeneration, retained-pack recovery, unified decoration permissions and Adaptive Window placement ownership.
changes: Retain the union of saved/helper IDs, active-pack inventory and prior staged inventory at every builder entry point. Never filter away required materials missing from the catalogue.

Snapshot and preflight all material metadata, shape/model bindings and PNGs before atomic replacement. Produce actionable per-material diagnostics and suspend cache/discovery writes during fallback recovery.
Check placement versus breaking rules separately, including environment and support/occupied cells. Use cancellable native pre-events for all removal paths and reject redirected placement checks.
Keep ZMA_Window items in their native placement path and share a versioned token-to-donor index for P and Q materials.
Separate integration sources/jar, remove two synthetic catalogue materials from ordinary packaging, and audit resource preservation and provenance.

Move old pack bytes intact and preserve the existing fail-closed rebuild/fallback mechanism. Retain both legacy and internal inventories in next-start builds.
Update the backup/rollback installer for worlds already blocked by client preflight. Target the installed 0.7.4 server and keep all asset bytes unchanged.
